<div class="bio-column">

<p class="intro-first">
Hello! I’m Jungsik Choi, a Ph.D. candidate in Sociology and Social Data Analytics at Penn State, where I am advised by <a href="https://www.danieldellaposta.com/" target="_blank">Daniel DellaPosta</a>. I earned my B.A. and M.A. in Sociology from Seoul National University.
</p>

<p>
My research examines how political institutions, historical change, and sociodemographic characteristics shape public opinion and media discourse about science, nation-states, and democracy.
</p>

<p>
My current work examines (1) how institutional contexts shape the divergent grounds on which scientific authority is legitimized across countries, (2) how U.S. news media construct symbolic hierarchies among foreign countries, and (3) how the organization of beliefs about democracy varies across countries.
</p>

<p>
In related work on collective intelligence, I study how social networks and the diversity of ideas shared on an online investing platform shape the accuracy of crowdsourced stock market predictions.
</p>

<p>
Across these projects, I draw on cross-national surveys, historical news archives, and social media data. My methods include regression modeling, computational text analysis, and network analysis.
</p>
